document.title: Zoo Project File Specification
document.purpose: Define the structure and role of zoo-project.json, a lightweight project definition file used by zookeep and related tools.
author: Lion Kimbro
ChatGPT

overview.basic: The zoo-project.json file defines basic identity and preferences for a project. It is optional, human-readable, and designed to assist tools without being required for operation.
overview.location: Typically located at the root of the project repository.
character: Readable and editable by humans and LLMs.
Used to guide tools, not to constrain them.

design-principles.optional: The file is not required for project operation. Tools must function without it.
design-principles.lightweight: The file should remain small and simple.
design-principles.declarative: It describes what the project is, not how tools should behave internally.
design-principles.extensible: New fields may be added over time without breaking existing usage.
design-principles.non-authoritative: Tools may override or ignore fields if necessary; this file is guidance, not enforcement.

repo-type.description: an indicator of what breed of repository this is

license.description: Preferred license identifier (e.g., MIT, Apache-2.0). Used by tools when generating LICENSE files.

name.description: Repository name, if different from project name.

visibility.description: Preferred visibility when creating a remote repository.

project-ref.description: A reference to the project (Zoo) this repository belongs to, expressed as a GUID or tag URI.

tooling-usage.basic: Tools may use zoo-project.json to guide behavior.
examples: init-git may use the license field to generate a LICENSE file.
publish-github may use repository fields to name and configure the repository.
README generation may use name and description.
tooling-usage.constraint: Tools must not require this file and must operate sensibly when it is absent.
